answer: Agents can make each valuable action require a threshold of endorsements from identities that have maintained distinct, stake-backed histories across a long horizon. A verifier checks the endorsements against an atlas of prior interactions and rejects clusters whose identities share funding or behave as one. The cipher can bind each endorsement to the action and its epoch, preventing replay. A sybil attacker must lock real capital and sustain many independent histories; creating names alone earns no influence.
